New plan: 

In my previous attempts, I focused on calculating the net displacement after each set of instructions. However, this approach led to incorrect conclusions. A more accurate method would be to analyze the instructions in terms of the total number of steps taken in each direction. 

To determine whether one would end up back at the starting point, I will calculate the total number of steps taken in each direction and compare them. If the total number of steps taken in one direction is equal to the total number of steps taken in the opposite direction, then the starting point is reached. 

In the case of the instructions "Always face forward. Take 10 steps left. Take 7 steps right. Take 4 steps right. Take 1 step left," I will recalculate the total number of steps taken in each direction:

- Left: 10 + 1 = 11 steps
- Right: 7 + 4 = 11 steps

Since the total number of steps taken in the left direction (11) is equal to the total number of steps taken in the right direction (11), the starting point is reached. 

Therefore, my new plan is to analyze the instructions in terms of the total number of steps taken in each direction and compare them to determine whether the starting point is reached.
